PIK.name: Glasgow Prestwick
PIK.fly: Ryanair flies here, mostly from Spain, Portugal and the Canaries when I last checked. I haven’t seen flights from other UK airports, so this one suits you if you are coming from abroad.

GLA.name: Glasgow
GLA.fly: The main airport for the west of Scotland. When I last checked you could fly in from London, Belfast, Bristol, Birmingham and plenty of Europe.

MAN.name: Manchester
MAN.fly: The biggest airport in the north, with flights from all over the UK, Europe and further away. If you are flying a long way, this is the one I would look at first.

LPL.name: Liverpool John Lennon
LPL.fly: A smaller, easy airport. When I last checked you could fly in from Belfast, the Isle of Man and a good spread of Europe.

BHX.name: Birmingham
BHX.fly: Right next to the railway. When I last checked you could fly in from Belfast, Edinburgh, Glasgow and Aberdeen, plus most of Europe.

CWL.name: Cardiff
CWL.fly: A small airport with a handful of UK and European routes, so please check it flies from near you before you plan around it.

BRS.name: Bristol
BRS.fly: Far more flights than Cardiff. When I last checked you could fly in from Edinburgh, Glasgow, Belfast and Newcastle, plus most of Europe.

STN.name: London Stansted
STN.fly: A big Ryanair airport. When I last checked you could fly in from Edinburgh and Belfast, and from most of Europe.

LTN.name: London Luton
LTN.fly: Mostly easyJet and Wizz Air. When I last checked you could fly in from Edinburgh, Glasgow and Belfast, plus a lot of Europe.

SEN.name: London Southend
SEN.fly: A small airport that is quick to get through. easyJet flies here from Europe, and from Edinburgh and Belfast too when I last checked.

SOU.name: Southampton
SOU.fly: A small airport with its own station. When I last checked you could fly in from Scotland, the north of England, Belfast and the Channel Islands.

LGW.name: London Gatwick
LGW.fly: Flights from all over the UK and the world. When I last checked that included Edinburgh, Glasgow, Belfast, Inverness and Jersey.

ayr.sub: The closest airport to any show on this page
steps: The airport has its own station, joined to the terminal by a covered walkway. ScotRail trains to Ayr take about 10 minutes and there are usually two an hour. You can’t buy a ticket at the station, so buy it online or on the train.
From Ayr station I would head down to Fort Street and through Wellington Square to the Esplanade. Allow 15 to 20 minutes.
Airport bus to Glasgow city centre
The Glasgow Airport Express, the 500, runs from outside the terminal into the city. Get off for Glasgow Central station.
ScotRail normally runs every 30 minutes and takes just over 50 minutes. There were extra trains on the 2026 show Saturday.
Allow 15 to 20 minutes from Ayr station, or a bit more in the crowds.

blackpool.sub: The station is inside the airport
steps: Manchester Airport station to Blackpool North
Northern trains run from the airport station to Blackpool North. If yours doesn’t run all the way through, change at Preston.
From Blackpool North I would walk down Talbot Road to North Pier, then south along the front to the Tower. Allow 15 minutes.

blackpool.sub: Bus to the station, then two trains
steps: The 80A and 86A run from the airport to Liverpool South Parkway station, about 3 miles away.
South Parkway to Liverpool Lime Street
A short hop into the city on any train to Lime Street.
Liverpool Lime Street to Blackpool North
Northern runs direct to Blackpool North in about an hour and a half.
Allow 15 minutes from Blackpool North to the Tower.

southport.sub: One bus, then one train all the way
steps: The 80A and 86A run from the airport to Liverpool South Parkway station, about 3 miles away.
Take the Northern line from South Parkway. It runs through the middle of Liverpool and on to Southport, so you can stay in your seat.
Along Lord Street and Nevill Street to the Promenade, about 10 minutes.
Take any train from the airport station into the city, to Manchester Piccadilly or Oxford Road.
Northern runs to Southport through Bolton and Wigan Wallgate. You’ll need to change at Wigan Wallgate if your train finishes there.
Along Lord Street and Nevill Street to the Promenade.

cosford.sub: Train from the airport, one change
steps: Air Rail Link to Birmingham International
The free people mover takes a couple of minutes from the terminal to Birmingham International station.
Birmingham International to Birmingham New Street
There are trains every few minutes and it takes about 10 to 15 minutes.
West Midlands Railway runs towards Shrewsbury and calls at Cosford. Trains are normally hourly on a Sunday.
The station is under 300 metres from the entrance. I would follow the stewards.
Air Rail Link to Birmingham International
The free people mover takes a couple of minutes from the terminal to the station.
Birmingham International to Birmingham New Street
About 10 to 15 minutes, with trains every few minutes.
Change onto the Cross City line and stay on to the end at Redditch.
The 247 between Redditch and Evesham stops right by the main entrance. There is no Sunday service, so I would book a taxi from Redditch for a Sunday.
The 905 links the terminal with Rhoose Cardiff International Airport station, a few minutes away.
Transport for Wales trains head west along the coast to Bridgend.
Change at Bridgend onto a main line train to Swansea.
I would head down through the city centre to Oystermouth Road and the promenade by the Civic Centre.
Airport Flyer to Bristol Temple Meads
The A1 Airport Flyer runs from the terminal to Bristol Temple Meads station.
Head through the Severn Tunnel into Wales. You will usually change at Cardiff Central for Swansea.
Down through the city centre to Oystermouth Road and the promenade.
The station is under the terminal. Trains to Cambridge take around 35 minutes.
For the Summer Air Show and the Battle of Britain Air Show, free shuttle buses run from stand 5 at the station to IWM Duxford. It takes about 30 minutes and there’s no need to book.
Or get off at Whittlesford Parkway
Some trains from Stansted stop at Whittlesford Parkway, the nearest station. It’s about a 30 minute walk across the busy A505, so I wouldn’t do it with young children.

shuttleworth.sub: Train to Bedford, then a taxi
steps: Luton DART to Luton Airport Parkway
The DART shuttle takes a few minutes from the terminal to the station.
Thameslink trains head north to Bedford in around 20 to 25 minutes.
Taxi from Bedford to Old Warden
Bedford is 9.5 miles from Shuttleworth, about 20 minutes by taxi. I would book it before you fly.
Or use the show shuttle from Biggleswade
Shuttleworth runs its own shuttle from Biggleswade station. From Luton that means going into London St Pancras, walking across to King’s Cross and coming back out, so it takes a lot longer.

gransden.sub: Train to Cambridge, then a taxi
steps: The station is under the terminal. Trains to Cambridge take around 35 minutes.
Taxi from Cambridge to the airfield
Cambridge is about 15 miles from Little Gransden and a taxi takes around 30 minutes. There’s no show shuttle, so I would book the taxi both ways.
The station is right outside the terminal. Take a Greater Anglia train towards London Liverpool Street and get off at Shenfield.
Change onto the Clacton train. Normally there’s one direct train an hour.
From the station, head down through the town centre to the seafront, then turn right. It’s 10 to 15 minutes.

clacton.sub: Coach to Colchester, then the train
steps: The 717 runs between Stansted Airport and Ipswich and calls at Colchester Coach Stop. Book in advance with National Express.
Greater Anglia takes about 29 minutes. The 74, 74B and 76 buses run to Clacton too.
Head down to the seafront and turn right.

riat.sub: Last leg to Boscombe Down not announced yet
steps: The station is a minute’s walk from the terminal. South Western Railway runs to Salisbury, and some journeys need a change at Southampton Central.
The organisers haven’t released the travel plan for the new airfield yet. I will add the last leg from Salisbury as soon as they do, so I would hold off booking flights until then.
The station is in the South Terminal. Redhill is the next main stop towards London.
Change at Redhill onto the line across to Tonbridge.
Change again onto a Southeastern train towards Ashford. Headcorn is a few stops along.
It is about a mile and a half along country lanes, so I would think about a taxi for this last stretch.

eastbourne.sub: One direct train from the airport
steps: Southern runs direct from the airport station to Eastbourne, so there are no changes.
Come out onto Terminus Road, head south through the town centre to the seafront, then turn right. It’s 10 to 15 minutes.
